title: Case Study 11: Right to Equality & Affirmative Action (Articles 14–18) (Article 14 — Writ Petition (Civil/Criminal))
legalTheme: Right to Equality & Affirmative Action (Articles 14–18) • Article 14 & Substantive Equality
factualMatrix: In a matter instituted before the Supreme Court of India (Article 32 Writ Jurisdiction), the Petitioner—an aggrieved citizen/association affected by a recent District Administration & Police Authority action—challenged the constitutionality and procedural validity of an impugned administrative circular and detention/restraint order touching upon Article 14 (Right to Equality & Affirmative Action (Articles 14–18)). 2. How does the principle of Right to Equality & Affirmative Action (Articles 14–18) (Substantive Equality) apply to the impugned administrative circular and detention/restraint order issued by the District Administration & Police Authority?

modelAnswer:
1. MAINTAINABILITY & THRESHOLD (Article 14): Under the constitutional scheme governing Right to Equality & Affirmative Action (Articles 14–18), a Writ Petition (Civil/Criminal) before the Supreme Court of India (Article 32 Writ Jurisdiction) is maintainable where a prima facie breach of Article 14 or statutory/constitutional limits is demonstrated. The Court evaluates threshold jurisdiction without permitting procedural technicalities to defeat substantive constitutional justice.

2. DOCTRINAL & STATUTORY ANALYSIS (Right to Equality & Affirmative Action (Articles 14–18)): Core constitutional framework under Right to Equality & Affirmative Action (Articles 14–18). Applying the core concept of 'Substantive Equality', the impugned administrative circular and detention/restraint order by the District Administration & Police Authority must satisfy legality, rational nexus, and proportionality. As reinforced by As settled in State of W.B. v. Anwar Ali Sarkar (1952), "Equality before the law" is of English origin (a negative concept indicating the absence of special privilege), whereas "Equal protection of the laws" is borrowed from Section 1 of the 14th Amendment of the U.S. Constitution (a positive concept pledging equal protection in similar circumstances).

3. PRECEDENT APPLICATION (State Sub-Quotas for Mahadalits & Creamy Layer Challenge) & RELIEF: Guided by State Sub-Quotas for Mahadalits & Creamy Layer Challenge, any executive or legislative overreach inconsistent with Article 14 is liable to be struck down or suitably moulded by appropriate directions. Further, Article 14 uses the word "person" ("The State shall not deny to any person equality before the law..."), which extends to both citizens and foreigners, as well as juristic/legal entities such as companies, statutory corporations, and registered societies (Chiranjit Lal Chowdhury v. Union of India).

Applying the core concept of 'Manifest Arbitrariness', the impugned administrative circular and detention/restraint order by the District Administration & Police Authority must satisfy legality, rational nexus, and proportionality.
